definitions.explanation: A district or neighborhood where geisha houses, teahouses, and traditional entertainment establishments are concentrated. Historically the center of traditional Japanese performing arts and hospitality.

examples.japanese: {京都|きょうと}には{有名|ゆうめい}な{花街|かがい}がある。
{花街|かがい}の{文化|ぶんか}を{守|まも}る{活動|かつどう}が{続|つづ}いている。
examples.english: Efforts to preserve the culture of the geisha districts continue.

examples.japanese: {祇園|ぎおん}は{日本|にほん}で{最|もっと}も{有名|ゆうめい}な{花街|かがい}で、{舞妓|まいこ}さんの{姿|すがた}を{見|み}ることができる。
examples.english: Gion is Japan's most famous geisha district, where you can see apprentice geisha.

notes:
FORMS:
{花|か} (flower) + {街|がい} (district, quarter). The 'flower' metaphor refers to the beauty and refinement of the arts practiced there.

CULTURAL NOTE:
Kyoto's five major {花街|かがい} are {祇園甲部|ぎおんこうぶ}, {祇園東|ぎおんひがし}, {先斗町|ぽんとちょう}, {上七軒|かみしちけん}, and {宮川町|みやがわちょう}. Tokyo also had its own {花街|かがい}, such as {新橋|しんばし} and {赤坂|あかさか}. These districts are associated with traditional arts including {日本舞踊|にほんぶよう}, {三味線|しゃみせん}, and the tea ceremony.

ALTERNATE READING:
Also read as はなまち, which is more colloquial.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {花街|かがい}の{文化|ぶんか} (culture of the geisha districts)
- {花街|かがい}の{伝統|でんとう} (traditions of the geisha districts)
- {京都|きょうと}の{花街|かがい} (Kyoto's geisha districts)
